query: How can sellers improve Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: sentiment
per_column.rationale: Sentiment is grounded and correctly read across samples, but it is a bare positive/negative flag that is largely redundant with the existing label_pos column (a perfect 125/125 split mirrors it), limiting genuine new analytical leverage for the improvement query.

per_column.name: mentioned_topics
per_column.rationale: A topic taxonomy is a strong axis for grouping reviews to identify improvement areas. However groundedness is weak: the doll review is tagged 'ease_of_use' (unsupported), the Eamon music rant is tagged 'sizing_fit' (nonsensical), and the book review tagged 'general_experience' loses the actual content signal. Several sample tags contradict or invent topics not present in the text.

per_column.name: seller_improvement_signal
per_column.rationale: This is the most directly query-aligned column, mapping reviews to actionable seller actions. But it inherits errors and over-asserts: it collapses all positives to 'maintain_current_quality' and lumps varied negatives into 'investigate_general_dissatisfaction'. The AMZ-0004 positive explicitly complains about a formulation change yet is tagged 'maintain_current_quality', misreading a stated negative.

per_column.name: review_length_bucket
per_column.rationale: Derivable and consistent with content length, but it is a generic text-length proxy that offers no analytical leverage for how sellers can improve satisfaction; adds no meaningful axis to group or model on for this query.

judge.rationale: The set contains two query-relevant axes (mentioned_topics, seller_improvement_signal) that genuinely support grouping reviews into actionable improvement areas, one redundant sentiment flag, and one low-value length bucket. Groundedness is the main weakness: multiple sample tags are invented or contradict the source (music rant as 'sizing_fit', doll review as 'ease_of_use', a positive with an explicit formulation complaint marked 'maintain_current_quality'), indicating unreliable extraction on off-taxonomy content.
